title: Weil restriction of constants and Frobenius powers
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. For $e\geq1$, put $k_e=\mathbf F_{q^e}\subset k$ and $X_{0,e}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_e$. Under the canonical identification $X_{0,e}\times_{k_e}k\simeq X$, the geometric Frobenius of the extended base is $g_X^e$. The iterated Weil isomorphism
$$\theta^{[e]}=\theta\circ Lg_X^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ L(g_X^{e-1})^*\theta$$
defines a lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal F^{(e)}=(M,\theta^{[e]})$ on $X_{0,e}$.
For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, the identity on the underlying coefficient cohomology identifies
$$\bigl(H_c^r(X,\mathcal F^{(e)}),F_{q^e}\bigr)\simeq\bigl(H_c^r(X,\mathcal F),F_q^e\bigr)$$
as Frobenius modules, with compact cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. If a closed point $z\in X_{0,e}$ maps to $x\in X_0$, the local geometric Frobenius on the stalk of $\mathcal F^{(e)}$ at $z$ is conjugate to
$$F_x^{[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]}$$
with the local-operator convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. For every real $w$, if $\mathcal F$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then $\mathcal F^{(e)}$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ relative to $k_e$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. No geometric connectedness or semisimplicity is assumed.

source.place: Second paragraph: local stalk Frobenius is a residue-degree power and the cohomology operator over the constant extension is F^e; made precise using the iterated Weil structure
